findings.title: No code computes or plots any reported figure or the derived tables (2, 5, Figs 2-13)
findings.claim: A deterministic scan of all 42 .py files finds 0 occurrences of plotting (matplotlib/savefig/plt/pie), 0 of any result/ASR aggregation, 0 of train-dataset-attribution or bigram-rank analysis, 0 of median-perplexity computation, and 0 notebooks; the pipeline ends at per-behavior `judge_output`/`filter_passed` in evaluate_completions.py.
findings.concern: None of the paper's figures (2a,2b,3-13) or its derived tables (Table 2 median-PPL numbers, Table 5 judge accuracy/FPR/FNR, and the filter-derivation AUC/FPR curves) can be reproduced, and the interpretability/train-dataset-attribution analysis that is a stated core contribution (Section 5.4, contribution bullet 4) has no code at all.
findings.resolution: Authors: please add the aggregation/analysis/plotting scripts (or notebooks) that turn the per-behavior CSVs into Tables 2-5 and Figures 2-13, including the train-dataset-attribution and bigram-rank code.
findings.reason: Re-ran check_missing_analysis_code.py fresh; output matches the quote exactly (0 hits for plotting/ASR-aggregation/attribution/median-PPL/notebooks across all 42 .py files; row idx=2 reads 'ASR / success-rate aggregation into a table,0,NO').

findings.title: Bigram LM construction from Dolma (1T tokens) is absent; only a gdown download of prebuilt counts
findings.claim: The N-gram counts (unigrams/bigrams parquet) are downloaded from two Google-Drive IDs; no repo code tokenizes the Dolma subset (MegaWika, Gutenberg, StackExchange, arXiv, Reddit, StarCoder, RefinedWeb), splits Dtrain/Dval, or counts N-grams (0 construction hits in the static scan).
findings.concern: Section 3.2's headline contribution ('we construct a lightweight bigram LM from the Dolma dataset based on 1T tokens') and the Dtrain/Dval split cannot be reproduced or verified; the downloaded parquets are even named `df_gutenberg_*` which is at odds with the seven-dataset subset the paper describes (though the hardcoded total ≈0.955T in ppl_filter.py:172 is consistent with ~1T tokens).
findings.resolution: Authors: please release the N-gram construction script (tokenization + counting + Dtrain/Dval split) and clarify the `gutenberg` filename vs the full Dolma subset used.
findings.paper_ref: Section 3.2 'Construction of the N-gram model'; Appendix C
findings.reason: download_unpack_ngrams.sh:6-8 match the quote verbatim (two gdown calls, no construction code); repo-wide scan confirms 0 ngram-construction hits; df_gutenberg_* parquet filenames (evaluate_completions.py:61,64) and ppl_filter.py:172 total_bigrams=955312057204 (~0.955T) both confirmed as claimed.

findings.title: 2,000-label human-evaluation dataset and judge-comparison code (Table 5 / Appendix B) not in repo
findings.claim: Appendix B / Table 5 report a human-evaluation study (2,000 responses labelled by two authors) comparing six judge models by Accuracy/FPR/FNR; the repo ships the judge *templates* (ppl_filter.py) but neither the 2,000 labels nor any script that computes the judge-vs-human agreement metrics.
findings.concern: The judge-selection claim ('Based on accuracy, for all our evaluations we use Llama2-13B (HarmBench)') and Table 5's numbers cannot be verified or reproduced from the repo.
findings.resolution: Authors: please release the 2,000 labelled responses and the script that computes each judge's Accuracy/FPR/FNR against the human labels.
findings.reason: paper_text.txt:1170 contains the quoted sentence verbatim ('we manually labeled 2,000 responses', Table 5 at line 1176); a repo-wide search for human-label/2000/FPR/FNR/judge-accuracy code found no genuine hits, confirming the labels and comparison script are absent from the repo.

findings.claim: Most result-affecting libraries (transformers, accelerate, numpy, tokenizers, vllm) are unpinned; environment.yml lists only python=3.10 and cudatoolkit; the pipeline also depends on an undocumented WORK_DIR env var and gated HF weights + two gdown links.
findings.concern: The paper itself notes bfloat16 numerical instabilities can 'significantly reduce ASR' (Appendix G), so unpinned transformers/vllm versions make the exact reported numbers hard to reproduce; the gdown/HF dependencies are also link-rot / access-gated.
findings.resolution: Authors: please pin the versions of transformers, accelerate, numpy, tokenizers and vllm (a full pip freeze), and document WORK_DIR and the N-gram artefact provenance.
findings.reason: requirements.txt:40-47 match the quote verbatim; environment.yml contains only python=3.10 and cudatoolkit as claimed; accelerate/numpy/tokenizers are confirmed unpinned (no version specifier) in requirements.txt.

findings.title: evaluate_completions.py applies the PPL filter to the clean instruction, not the jailbreak
findings.claim: In the shipped Step-4 evaluation, `user_message` is `df["behavior"]` (evaluate_completions.py:50), the clean HarmBench instruction that is also passed to the judge as the goal (line 82); the actual jailbreak is a separate column `best_msg`/`test_case` (set in aggregate_csv.py:85-90 and logged as `best_msg = insert_adv_string(orig_msg, adv)` in main_adaptive_attack.py:262).
findings.concern: Threat-model condition 1 constrains the *jailbreak* x_jailbreak (behavior ⊕ optimized suffix); applying the filter to the clean instruction, which is natural low-perplexity text, makes `filter_passed` nearly always True and does not test the object the threat model constrains — so the repo's only post-hoc filter check (used to reproduce Table 3's '+F' column) evaluates the wrong text.
findings.resolution: Authors: should the filter be applied to `df["best_msg"]` (the jailbreak) rather than `df["behavior"]`? If the published '+F' numbers were produced by filtering the jailbreak, please ship that computation, since the repo's version filters the instruction.
findings.reason: evaluate_completions.py:87-89 match the quote verbatim; line 50 confirms user_message traces to df['behavior'], line 82 confirms the same value is passed to the judge as the goal; aggregate_csv.py:85-90 and main_adaptive_attack.py:262 confirm best_msg/test_case is the separate jailbreak column; re-ran check_filter_target_column.py, which reproduces the same conclusion.

findings.title: Implemented window perplexity adds an initial-unigram term absent from paper Eq. 3
findings.quote:
if conditional_probs:
    total_log_prob = np.sum(np.log(conditional_probs))
    # Add the log probability of the first unigram to start the chain properly
    total_log_prob += np.log(unigram_probs[0])
    perplexity = np.exp(-total_log_prob / len(bigrams))
findings.claim: The code computes PPL = exp(-(log P(w1) + Σ_{i} log P(w_{i+1}|w_i)) / (W-1)); it adds the marginal log-prob of the first token (line 504) and divides by the number of bigrams W-1.
findings.concern: Paper Eq. 3 (for N=2) defines PPL_2 as the product of conditional probabilities from i=2..W raised to 1/(W-1), i.e. WITHOUT the initial log P(w1) term; the implemented metric therefore differs from the documented formula by a P(w1)^{-1/(W-1)} factor. Both are valid perplexity-like scores and the threshold 38,276 was calibrated with this code, so the impact is a faithfulness/documentation gap rather than an error.
findings.resolution: Authors: please align Eq. 3 with the implementation (either add the initial-unigram term to the equation or drop it from the code), so the documented metric matches the one used for the threshold.
findings.reason: ppl_filter.py:501-505 match the quote verbatim; paper Eq. 3 (paper_text.txt:210-222) defines PPL_N as the (W-N+1)-th root of the product of conditional probabilities from i=N..W with no initial-unigram term, confirming the code's added log(unigram_probs[0]) term is not part of the documented formula.
